problem_text:
A municipality aims to devise a strategy for curbing nutrient runoff from several agricultural plots into a nearby watershed. Initially, no mitigation practices have been implemented.
The profile of each agricultural plot is as follows:
* For Plot A, runoff coefficient is 1.843, cultivated area is 90.239.
* For Plot B, runoff coefficient is 2.867, cultivated area is 105.197.
* For Plot C, runoff coefficient is 1.262, cultivated area is 258.687.
* For Plot D, runoff coefficient is 2.371, cultivated area is 98.582.
* For Plot E, runoff coefficient is 2.759, cultivated area is 95.339.
* For Plot F, runoff coefficient is 1.36, cultivated area is 249.915.
* For Plot G, runoff coefficient is 1.532, cultivated area is 263.063.
* For Plot H, runoff coefficient is 2.115, cultivated area is 262.847.
* For Plot I, runoff coefficient is 1.781, cultivated area is 283.092.

To reduce nutrient loss, several best management practices (BMPs) are available, each with a specific effectiveness:
* Implementing BMP1 reduces nutrient loss by 10%
* Implementing BMP2 reduces nutrient loss by 53%
* Implementing BMP3 reduces nutrient loss by 46%
* Implementing BMP4 reduces nutrient loss by 67%
* Implementing BMP5 reduces nutrient loss by 85%
* Implementing BMP6 reduces nutrient loss by 82%
* Implementing BMP7 reduces nutrient loss by 32%
* Implementing BMP8 reduces nutrient loss by 51%
* Implementing BMP9 reduces nutrient loss by 64%

Adopting a BMP on a plot incurs an implementation cost per unit of cultivated area. The cost matrix for all plot–BMP combinations is provided below:

| Plot \ BMP | BMP1 | BMP2 | BMP3 | BMP4 | BMP5 | BMP6 | BMP7 | BMP8 | BMP9 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Plot A | 34.361 | 134.54 | 29.009 | 127.708 | 181.023 | 70.379 | 95.623 | 127.105 | 68.078 |
| Plot B | 120.992 | 117.455 | 79.254 | 70.103 | 91.378 | 10.918 | 56.773 | 52.09 | 150.565 |
| Plot C | 92.864 | 169.621 | 35.518 | 149.265 | 176.798 | 97.941 | 78.161 | 68.04 | 114.818 |
| Plot D | 43.396 | 125.259 | 169.941 | 173.156 | 36.6 | 112.337 | 60.015 | 178.404 | 24.528 |
| Plot E | 24.326 | 13.54 | 106.364 | 15.927 | 120.559 | 86.976 | 122.107 | 182.198 | 114.803 |
| Plot F | 113.259 | 199.758 | 99.7 | 157.287 | 79.506 | 52.428 | 156.708 | 149.313 | 65.29 |
| Plot G | 98.293 | 106.978 | 85.389 | 105.412 | 135.909 | 171.117 | 163.243 | 126.667 | 41.51 |
| Plot H | 107.686 | 94.782 | 44.038 | 190.255 | 135.289 | 193.87 | 149.825 | 101.866 | 78.171 |
| Plot I | 51.576 | 102.652 | 21.944 | 80.193 | 18.134 | 49.287 | 182.468 | 78.638 | 99.238 |

The municipality must decide which BMPs to apply to each plot (plots may adopt multiple BMPs concurrently), and a plot may also remain partially untreated if required. The objective is to ensure that the total nutrient runoff is reduced by at least a fraction P = 0.427 of the baseline amount, while minimizing the total implementation expenditure.
